title: Customer Edge Approval SLA and Evidence Retention (PRD notes)
content:
Purpose:

This is a working PRD-level draft capturing proposed behavior for approval orchestration and the immutable evidence retention model for Customer-Managed (VPC / on-prem) deployments. Focus: define SLAs, wire up an evidence bundle format suitable for audits/forensics, and describe integration points for customer-managed networking (mutual TLS, webhook handshakes, and KMS attestations).

Problem statement:
- Customers deploying Redwood Private expect: (a) deterministic approval gating for network/operator-initiated changes, (b) cryptographically verifiable evidence for every approval decision, and (c) configurable retention policies to meet their compliance needs.
- Today we have ad-hoc logs and sampling; this is insufficient for regulated customers that require full-chronicled proofs for change requests and timely SLAs on decisioning.

Goals:
1) Define an Approval SLA surface (latency percentiles, fallback behaviors, escalation windows).
2) Create a compact, versioned Evidence Bundle format (immutable, verifiable, exportable).
3) Specify integration contract for customer-managed networks (mutual auth, permitted endpoints, routing hints).
4) Provide operator UX + API primitives to manage retention tiers and export bundles for external archives.
5) Ensure the model supports offline forensics (replayable traces) and cross-checks with telemetry and tokenized references to KV caches.

Non-goals:
- Implementing full crypto-hardware backed attestations (HSM integration will be a follow-up).
- Replacing customer-side SIEM or existing change-control tools; instead we want safe, exportable proofs that can be ingested by those tools.

Personas:
- Platform Operator (customer): needs quick approvals, clear audit trail, ability to export proofs to internal compliance team.
- Redwood Operator: needs predictable fallbacks and visibility when customer-managed hooks are unavailable.
- Security Auditor: needs immutable evidence and canonical event ordering.

High-level flow (operator-initiated network change):
1) Operator issues a change via Console / API specifying target scope (tenant-id, operator-id, change-delta).
2) Redwood creates a provisional Change Record with state=awaiting-approval and emits an approval webhook to customer-approved endpoint(s).
3) Customer approval system responds with signed-assertion or denies. If signed-assertion, Redwood validates signature (mTLS + key id) and transitions to state=approved.
4) On approval, Redwood applies change, records pre/post snapshots, and writes an Evidence Bundle (see format).
5) If approval endpoint unavailable or timed out, Redwood follows configured fallback: auto-approve (customer configured), escalate to Redwood Ops, or fail.

Approval SLA surface (proposal):
- Defined per-customer with default: P50=1s, P95=2s, P99=10s for in-process decisions when approval is automated (local policy).
- For customer-synchronous approvals (webhook): soft SLA: P50=200ms network RTT + customer-processing; enforcement: Redwood enforces a decision timeout window (default 60s) after which fallback triggers.
- Escalation windows: after timeout N (configurable, default 60s) escalate to on-call or secondary approver.
- SLA clauses in Dedicated/Private contracts: guaranteed decisionability for policy-driven approvals; human approvals are best-effort and cannot be SLA-backed unless under managed service agreement.

Evidence Bundle (versioned format v0.1):
- Purpose: single-file exportable artifact that contains a canonical, replayable representation of a change and its approval lifecycle.
- Composition (flat list of fields):
  - bundle_id: GUID string
  - version: "0.1"
  - created_at: ISO8601
  - change_id: GUID
  - tenant_id: string
  - initiator: operator_id
  - action_summary: short text
  - before_snapshot_ref: SHA256 hex
  - after_snapshot_ref: SHA256 hex
  - diff_patch: text (unified diff or JSON patch; base64-encoded if binary)
  - approval_events: list of event_ids (ordered by timestamp)
  - event_log: list of flat event strings (timestamp | actor | action | outcome | signature_ref)
  - signatures: list of signature records (sig_id | signer | key_id | signature_b64)
  - attestation_chain: list of key references (keystore ids / key rotation metadata)
  - telemetry_refs: list of trace ids / span ids
  - retention_tier: string (short|medium|long)
  - export_checksum: SHA256(bundled-blob)
  - canonical_ordering_proof: Merkle-root hex (optional)

Notes on evidence format: bundle is intentionally flat and compact; large snapshots are stored externally (object store) with a reference hash in the bundle to avoid duplication. The bundle file itself should be gzipped JSON lines or CBOR to optimize size. All signatures in the bundle are represented as simple text entries (key id, base64 sig).

Retention tiers (configurable per-tenant):
- short: 30 days (default for dev/test tenants)
- medium: 1 year (default for most customers)
- long: 7 years (for regulated customers)
- custom: customer-specified S3/GCS archive target + TTL

Retention semantics:
- Bundles are retained according to tier, with immutability guarantees while retained.
- Deletion is a two-step process: (1) mark-for-deletion, (2) physical removal after retention window; both steps logged and reversible within a short grace period (e.g., 7 days) for recovery.
- Exports to customer-provided archive are verified (checksum match) prior to local deletion.

Customer-managed network integration (contract):
- Authentication: mutual TLS + key id header. Our webhook client will present an identity cert; customer side must present a response signed-by-(customer key) or use mTLS session.
- Endpoint discovery: customer provides a DNS name or IP + credential bundle during onboarding. We support dynamic endpoint failover lists.
- Handshake: initial challenge/response to verify key ownership; Redwood stores key_id + fingerprint for future signature validation.
- Retry logic: exponential backoff for webhooks up to configured attempts (default 5) before fallback.
- Observability: Redwood sends structured diagnostics and a correlation id for each webhook attempt (for joint troubleshooting).

API primitives (proposed minimal set):
- POST /v1/private/change-requests -> create change & returns change_id
- GET /v1/private/change-requests/{id} -> change state + event log
- POST /v1/private/change-requests/{id}/approve -> internal use; accepts signed assertion (sig_b64 + key_id)
- GET /v1/private/evidence-bundles/{bundle_id} -> download bundle (gzipped)
- POST /v1/private/evidence-exports -> trigger copy to customer archive (returns export_job_id)
- GET /v1/private/metrics/approval-latency -> per-tenant SLA metrics (p50/p95/p99)

Operator UX (console):
- Change request list with filters (state, retention tier, initiator)
- Quick-approve: place-holder for customers that have delegated approval to Redwood policy (shows policy triggers and risk score)
- Export UI: run immediate bundle export, see progress, verify checksum, and schedule deletion
- Forensics view: read-only replay of event_log, associated telemetry links, and download buttons for snapshots and bundle

Forensics & replayability:
- Evidence Bundles must contain ordered event_log so a reviewer can replay the change deterministically (apply before_snapshot + diff_patch -> after_snapshot).
- Telemetry_refs should map to trace spans stored in our observability pipeline so we can correlate performance/latency with the change lifecycle.

Monitoring & metrics:
- Approval latency histograms per-tenant and per-approval-type
- Webhook failure rates, retry counts, and endpoint RTTs
- Evidence bundle generation latency and export success rates
- Retention quota usage and upcoming deletions alerts

Security & compliance considerations:
- Bundles marked immutable: once created they cannot be altered except via a clear and auditable append-only meta (retention state changes)
- Encryption: at-rest encryption using customer-provided KMS keys for private deployments is preferred. Keys referenced in attestation_chain must include rotation metadata.
- Access control: RBAC for who can view/download evidence bundles; granular permissions for export and delete
- PII minimization: bundles should avoid embedding raw sensitive payloads; prefer hashed refs and controlled snapshot retrieval with consent.

Failure modes and fallbacks:
- Webhook unreachable: fallback per-customer config (auto-approve | escalate | deny)
- Signature validation fails: mark as suspicious, escalate, and optionally quarantine change
- Bundle generation failure: try synchronous retry then async background job; if both fail, send alert and attach minimal event_log to change record

Open questions:
- Do we require cryptographic signing from customer-side for every approval, or allow lightweight HTTP assertions for lower-tier customers? (tradeoff: verifiability vs friction)
- Do we enforce a global maximum bundle size and offload large binary snapshots automatically? Threshold proposed: 50MB
- Should we offer HSM-backed signing for Redwood-signed attestations in high-compliance plans?
- Retention policy edge-cases for legal holds and eDiscovery requests: required extension flows?

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Default evidence bundle format documented and implemented for change requests in private deployments
- Webhook integration with mTLS + signed assertion support working end-to-end
- Console shows change request list, forensics view, and bundle download
- Metrics collected for approval latency and webhook reliability; basic alerts for failure modes

Milestones & next steps:
- 2025-01-15: Finalize evidence bundle v0.1 schema and approval SLA definitions
- 2025-02-01: Implement API endpoints + webhook client with mTLS
- 2025-03-01: Console forensics view + bundle download
- 2025-04-01: Retention management + export-to-customer-archive feature

Appendix (implementation notes):
- Prefer CBOR/gzip for bundles to keep size down and support streaming verification
- Use Merkle roots for canonical ordering if we need succinct cross-bundle proofs in the future
- Consider optional JSON-LD framing for easier ingestion by customer compliance systems

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Sync with SRE on archival requirements and object-store lifecycle policies (Jira: JIRA-PD-987)
- Draft contract language for SLA treatment of human approvals (legal input required)
- Prototype signed-assertion format and push a small test harness for customers to adopt quickly

References and links:
- Internal: CONFLUENCE-1234 (evidence-bundle-design)
- Implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/approval-service/pull/221

Reviewed: Luca Martinez (engineering), Jin Park (security)
